first_keys.title: The first grocery list
first_keys.text: The fridge contains a lemon, mustard and unreasonable optimism. A friend offers to split a proper shop.

choices.label: Cook a shared batch
choices.result: There is food for the week, and someone to complain about the dishes with.

choices.label: Plan around what I have
choices.result: The lemon becomes an ingredient rather than a lifestyle.

choices.label: Buy convenience for tonight
choices.result: A hot meal saves an exhausted evening, but costs more.

first_keys.title: A rattling window
first_keys.text: The flat loses heat. My friend knows a repair contact; the landlord needs a clear report.

choices.label: Document it and ask for repair
choices.result: A careful account makes the request harder to dismiss.

choices.label: Arrange a modest repair
choices.result: I pay for a practical repair and keep its receipt.

choices.label: Make do for now
choices.result: I keep the money, but the uncomfortable room takes a toll.

first_keys.title: The invitation
first_keys.text: Dinner with a friend falls on a night when I planned to prepare applications. Neither plan is silly.

choices.label: Share dinner, then shorten the application list
choices.result: We keep the connection and a realistic work plan.

choices.label: Keep the work evening; propose another date
choices.result: My friend understands a specific alternative better than a vague excuse.

choices.label: Stay home and rest
choices.result: The quiet helps; it does not maintain the friendship for me.

first_keys.title: Something that is mine
first_keys.text: The apartment still looks like a waiting room. I can afford one small change, not a showroom.

choices.label: Host a bring-your-own-chair evening
choices.result: The place acquires stories before it acquires matching furniture.

choices.label: Buy one useful lamp
choices.result: A small useful purchase makes the evenings calmer.

choices.label: Keep the money for the cushion
choices.result: An unspent lamp is not glamorous, but a buffer matters.

second_act.title: The blank line
second_act.text: An application asks what I have done lately. I have more life experience than polished evidence.

choices.label: Build a small honest work sample
choices.result: A concrete example gives me something truthful to discuss.

choices.label: Ask my friend to review the wording
choices.result: An outside reader spots a strength I had dismissed.

choices.label: Send a shorter application now
choices.result: I avoid endless preparation, while accepting a thinner application.

second_act.title: A timetable with teeth
second_act.text: Learning, applications and ordinary chores all want the same evenings.

choices.label: Protect a small regular learning slot
choices.result: A manageable schedule beats the heroic one I would abandon.

choices.label: Pay for help with one household task
choices.result: Delegation buys breathing room, at a real cost.

choices.label: Take a recovery week
choices.result: A pause is useful, but no qualification appears by magic.

second_act.title: An introduction
second_act.text: A friend offers an introduction, but cannot promise an employer will hire me.

choices.label: Prepare and accept the introduction
choices.result: We keep the promise small and the preparation specific.

choices.label: Practise together before deciding
choices.result: The conversation improves without turning a friend into an employment agency.

choices.label: Keep applying independently
choices.result: I preserve my independence and take the uncertainty with it.

second_act.title: The shape of success
second_act.text: My friend asks what a good second act would actually look like. A higher salary is only one answer.

choices.label: Make room for work and people
choices.result: A sustainable aim includes a life outside the job title.

choices.label: Keep learning without rushing the title
choices.result: The next skill can be useful before the next promotion.

choices.label: Prioritise stability this year
choices.result: An ordinary steady year is allowed to count.

small_world.title: The spare seat
small_world.text: A familiar cafe has one spare chair and a notice for a local reading circle.

choices.label: Invite my friend and try one meeting
choices.result: A small invitation makes the place feel less anonymous.

choices.label: Have a quiet catch-up instead
choices.result: Belonging does not require a club badge.

choices.label: Keep an evening to myself
choices.result: Solitude helps tonight; the connection waits for another day.

small_world.title: Too much volunteered
small_world.text: A neighbourhood organiser assumes I can help every weekend. I cannot.

choices.label: Offer one specific shift
choices.result: A limited promise is more useful than an impossible one.

choices.label: Contribute supplies instead of time
choices.result: The help has a budget and leaves my weekends intact.

choices.label: Say no and protect my energy
choices.result: I keep a boundary and lose this particular shared occasion.

small_world.title: Different memories
small_world.text: My friend and I remember an awkward evening differently. It is tempting to prove a winner.

choices.label: Ask what stayed with them
choices.result: I learn why the evening mattered, without agreeing on every detail.

choices.label: Take a walk and leave the dispute open
choices.result: We can keep each other without completing a courtroom argument.

choices.label: Change the subject tonight
choices.result: The evening stays easy; the unresolved feeling stays too.

small_world.title: A tradition small enough to keep
small_world.text: We want something regular, but nobody wants a second unpaid job as social coordinator.

choices.label: A monthly potluck with shared organising
choices.result: The routine belongs to everyone, not one exhausted host.

choices.label: A casual walk when our weeks fit
choices.result: A flexible tradition makes room for changing lives.

choices.label: Keep spontaneous meetings
choices.result: There is less pressure and fewer dependable occasions.
